subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a synchronous plugin-facing config pre-apply veto for persisted config writes, and what ordering, metadata, and failure semantics should it expose?
rationale: This defines a public plugin API around security-sensitive persisted config, auth, provider, and SecretRef-adjacent writes, so automation cannot safely choose the trust boundary or permanent SDK contract.

options.title: Design the API first
options.body: Keep this issue open, settle hook ordering and metadata in the config validation/mutation direction, then implement the agreed SDK contract with regression tests.

options.title: Rely on built-in validation
options.body: Decide not to add a plugin veto and rescope or close this around the existing schema, SecretRef, baseHash, destructive-array, and agent-tool guards.

options.title: Limit to agent tool writes
options.body: Add a narrower guard for model-initiated config writes, accepting that other persisted config writers remain outside the plugin veto path.

recommendation.title: Design the API first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, settle hook ordering and metadata in the config validation/mutation direction, then implement the agreed SDK contract with regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They already provided the clearest product-routing comment for this issue and have recent history on the config write boundary.
